newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Six Indonesia officers convicted for April protest.
newsitem.headline: Six Indonesia officers convicted for April protest.

text.p: Six Indonesian army officers have been sentenced to up to three months and 15 days jail for exceeding orders in dealing with a student protest in April, the official Antara news agency said on Sunday.

The military court in Ujung Pandang, provincial capital of South Sulawesi, convicted on Saturday three artillery officers, all second lieutenants, for intentionally exceeding official orders and sentenced them to three months jail.
In a separate trial, three other second lieutenants from a cavalry unit were sentenced to three months and 15 days jail under the same charges.
All those convicted were platoon leaders sent to supervise a student protest over rises in the price of bus fares held at Indonesian Muslim University in Ujung Pandang.

They are part of a group of 12 soldiers being court martialled over the incident, in which the military admited three students drowned in a river while fleeing troops. Human rights lawyers say six died in the incident.

Military prosecutors had asked for five and six months jail respectively for the two groups. The report did not say whether the men had been in custody since being charged. All those convicted said they would appeal, it added.

The report said the troops had been given guidelines to avoid physical contact with the university students as well as not provoke emotions. It said the convicted officers provoked a situation that led to a physical clash.
After an investigation, the official human rights commission reported in May that it had found the soldiers had violated human rights in their handling of the bus fare protests.
